title: Round the VFX checker detail/reason so an over-budget cost never reads as its cap
body:
## Summary
itemsVfxWithinBudget prints the GPU cost with toFixed(1), so 0.85 ms against a 0.8 ms cap reads "0.8 / 0.8 ms" and "VFX cost 0.8 ms exceeds the 0.8 ms budget".

## Description
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/itemsBespokeCheckers.ts:149 (detail) and :154 (reason) format cost with toFixed(1). This round fixed the bespoke copy and view (b24dad08, formatGpuMs in src/components/layout-lab/steps/itemsSteps.ts), but the checker lives in catalog-acceptance, outside this round's paths, and the banner detail still shows "0.8 / 0.8 ms" beside the corrected why. Fixed: move formatGpuMs into the checker module and have itemsSteps import it.

## Flow
- seed VFX {variants:[1], cost:0.85, cap:0.8}
- banner detail reads "0.8 / 0.8 ms" under PENDING (seen in the b24dad08 red-run output)
- fix: cap-aware precision in the checker; itemsSteps imports it

## Expected impact
An over-budget step no longer shows a cost equal to its cap. Nothing graded can break: detail and reason are display strings.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the checker detail never prints cost == cap when cost != cap
Before: 1 of 1 over-budget sample (0.85/0.8) prints "0.8 / 0.8 ms"
After: predicted "0.85 / 0.8 ms" (same formatter as the fixed copy)
Method: simulation - outside this round's paths, so not built; the copy-side twin went red to green under a gate
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/itemsBespokeCheckers.ts:149 `${cost.toFixed(1)} / ${cap} ms`
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/itemsBespokeCheckers.ts:154 `VFX cost ${cost.toFixed(1)} ms exceeds the ${cap} ms budget`
node: (0.85).toFixed(1) === "0.8"

title: Retire the six unrouted bespoke Items step UIs and their shadowed specs/copy
body:
## Summary
Since 2026-09-29 the six shared Items labels render through ArchetypeStep. ItemConceptBrief, ItemEconomy, ItemIcon2D, ItemTooltip, ItemTestGate, ItemPackaging and their ITEM_STEP_SPECS accept/copy bodies are still in the tree with no product consumer.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/index.ts:41 returns null for every non-bespoke items label, so the six components in ITEM_STEP_COMPONENTS (index.ts:19-23) never render. withItemFixCopy (steps/shared/itemFixCopy.ts) is used only by the bespoke frames, so briefCopy, economyCopy, iconCopy, tooltipCopy, gateCopy and packagingCopy (itemsSteps.ts) are reached only by tests. These unused bodies have drifted: the bespoke Economy accept reads Number(data.target) and prints "~NaN% below" for an artifact with no target (economyCopy); tooltipCopy reads data.fields while its accept reads data.tooltip.*; and the bespoke Test Gate grades registry-shaped Economy data with the bespoke Economy checker, which always returns pending. The 2026-09-29 note says the components "stay in the tree, unrouted" on purpose, so retiring them is the operator's call. Rule 4b and itemsLabelOwner still need the 13 ITEM_STEP_SPECS keys, but the produce/accept/view bodies could shrink to the 7 bespoke-owned labels.

## Flow
- grep consumers of the six components: index.ts plus 2 tests (ItemArt.gallery, itemGateVerdictLayers)
- decide: keep as reference, or retire
- if retired: keep the 13 label keys, drop the 6 bodies and components, point the tests at ArchetypeStep, keep items-spec-duality green

## Expected impact
About 400 LOC of unreachable UI and grading logic stops drifting from the live registry spec. Risk: tests that render these components directly need to be pointed elsewhere.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - remove code with zero product consumers
Before: 6 components + 6 accept bodies + 6 copy functions with 0 product consumers (grep)
After: 0 (by construction once removed)
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep run this round; removal not attempted because it contradicts a recorded keep decision
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
src/components/layout-lab/steps/index.ts:39-41 "The six shared labels' bespoke components stay in the tree, unrouted (2026-09-29)" + `if (catalogId === 'items' && itemsLabelOwner(stepName) !== 'bespoke') return null;`
grep ItemConceptBrief|ItemEconomy|ItemTooltip|ItemTestGate|ItemPackaging|ItemIcon2D -> steps/index.ts + own files + 2 tests
grep withItemFixCopy -> StaticStepFrame.tsx, GenerativeStepFrame.tsx only
instrument: zero-consumer grep plus the itemsUnionSteps / items-spec-duality suites after removal

title: Select the Items Test Gate by label, not by the hardcoded index 11
body:
## Summary
e2e/catalog-items-reference.spec.ts selects the Test Gate with selectStep(page, 11), a hand-maintained position in an 18-step union.

## Description
e2e/catalog-items-reference.spec.ts:62 hardcodes index 11, and its comment derives that number from ITEM_STEP_NAMES order. The same file already derives ITEMS_STEPS from catalogManifest (line 25). If a step is inserted before Test Gate in either spec, the walk would select the wrong step and still assert `deferred`, a status several steps reach. Fixed: `selectStep(page, ITEMS_STEPS.indexOf('Test Gate'))` plus an expect that the index is >= 0.

## Flow
- add a bespoke step before Test Gate
- the spec selects whatever now sits at index 11
- fix: derive the index from ITEMS_STEPS

## Expected impact
The reference e2e keeps testing the Test Gate when the union changes. Only the spec changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no hand-maintained step positions in the reference walk
Before: 1 hardcoded index
After: 0
Method: simulation - needs the Playwright run, which the director owns
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: e2e/catalog-items-reference.spec.ts:58-62 "Test Gate is the 12th step (index 11)" ... `await selectStep(page, 11);`
instrument: npm run test:e2e -- e2e/catalog-items-reference.spec.ts green with the derived index

title: Assert persisted verdict + direction in the Items reference walk, as the walker does
body:
## Summary
The generic walker checks each step's persisted server row and that the produce direction lands verbatim. The Items reference spec checks only the on-screen banner, so items is the one pipeline whose persisted verdict is never asserted end to end.

## Description
e2e/catalog-pipeline-walker.spec.ts:83-84 calls expectPersistedConfigComplete and expectPersistedDirection for every step. items is in WALKER_SKIP (e2e/helpers/pipeline-coverage.ts:10), and e2e/catalog-items-reference.spec.ts:40-52 reads only acceptanceStatus(page). So if an Items step persists `fail` while its banner shows `pass` (the judge-bridged gap the walker header documents), nothing catches it. Fixed: for each step, type a unique direction and call the same two helpers with step label = ITEMS_STEPS[i].

## Flow
- walk items via the reference spec
- add the two persisted assertions per step
- expect 18 x 2 soft assertions

## Expected impact
The reference pipeline gets the same server-truth check as the other catalogs. A real persisted fail can now turn the spec red, which is the point.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - persisted-truth coverage for the reference pipeline
Before: 0 of 18 items steps asserted on the persisted row
After: 18 of 18
Method: simulation - needs e2e
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
e2e/catalog-pipeline-walker.spec.ts:83-84 expectPersistedConfigComplete / expectPersistedDirection
e2e/catalog-items-reference.spec.ts:40-52 banner-only loop
instrument: Playwright reference spec run against the hermetic e2e DB

title: Record the Items reference walk in walk-status.json so the guard can see it rot
body:
## Summary
The validate-time walk-success guard reads e2e/walk-status.json, but only the generic walker writes that file and items is skipped there. A broken Items reference walk never turns validate red.

## Description
e2e/helpers/walk-status.ts writeWalkStatus records only walker pipelines, and pipeline-e2e-coverage.test.ts:70-78 checks only non-skipped pipelines. The items reference spec records nothing, so the Rule 5 rot signal is blind to exactly the reference pipeline. Fixed: after a green run the reference spec records an entry (e.g. `reference: {items: <ISO>}` or a sibling file), and the guard asserts one exists for every WALKER_SKIP entry whose reason names a bespoke spec.

## Flow
- break an items step so the reference spec fails
- validate stays green today
- fix: record the reference walk and assert it

## Expected impact
Rot in the reference pipeline shows up in npm run validate. Risk: the guard stays red until the director re-runs e2e once.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - walk-success signal covers every pipeline
Before: items: no recorded walk, 0 guard assertions
After: 1 recorded walk asserted
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: guard test plus one director e2e run

title: Correct the stale "13 bespoke step UIs" in WALKER_SKIP and ITEMS_SPEC_DUALITY
body:
## Summary
WALKER_SKIP.items and ITEMS_SPEC_DUALITY.reason still say the lab renders 13 bespoke step UIs + 5 registry-only labels. Since 2026-09-29 it renders 7 bespoke UIs + 11 registry ArchetypeSteps.

## Description
e2e/helpers/pipeline-coverage.ts:10-19 (reason and comment) and the ITEMS_SPEC_DUALITY.reason in src/components/layout-lab/catalogManifest.ts ("The 13 bespoke labels key the on-screen step UIs") were written before itemsLabelOwner. The e2e spec header already gives the 7/11 split. Only the reason text changes, and walk-status compares only WALKER_SKIP keys (pipeline-e2e-coverage.test.ts:85), so no recorded walk is invalidated. catalogManifest.ts belongs to catalog-pipeline-state, and pipeline-coverage.ts is not in this context's file list.

## Flow
- read WALKER_SKIP.items
- compare with the itemsLabelOwner counts (7 bespoke / 11 registry)
- reword both strings

## Expected impact
Anyone reading the skip reason gets the real screen composition. Nothing graded changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - docs match code
Before: 2 strings state 13 bespoke UIs
After: 0
Method: probe - counted via itemsLabelOwner this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
e2e/helpers/pipeline-coverage.ts:19 'the lab renders the UNION of both items specs (13 bespoke step UIs + the 5 registry-only labels)'
src/components/layout-lab/steps/index.ts:37-41 six shared labels unrouted
instrument: a test deriving the bespoke-UI count from itemsLabelOwner and asserting the reason names it

title: Derive the Items Economy power score from the entity's own Damage step
body:
## Summary
The registered Economy produce hardcodes Iron Longsword's power breakdown (dpsPower 10.0) for every item, so powerScore and pricePowerRatio ignore that item's own Damage step.

## Description
In the Economy produce in src/lib/catalog/pipelines/items.ts, powerBreakdown = { dpsPower: 10.0, implicitAccuracyPower: 1.8, affixPower: 0 }, and its comment "base DPS 12.5 (avg dmg 10 x APS 1.25)" contradicts the Damage step's own 15 x 0.8333. Effective (diablo/kotor) items with real damage ranges get the same 11.8 power. This round fixed the tooltip twin through damageStepProduce (ca396b98), and Economy can derive dpsPower = damage.baseDPS x 0.8 the same way. sumReconciles stays green. pricePowerRatio becomes item-specific and may fall outside the band for some seeds; that is the honest result, but it can move walker statuses.

## Flow
- produce Economy for item-lightsaber and item-1
- both report powerScore 11.8
- fix: dpsPower from damageStepProduce(e).data.damage.baseDPS

## Expected impact
Economy acceptance starts reflecting the item being priced. Risk: some seeded items may now fail the 0.8-1.2 band, and those status changes need a walker run.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authority per quantity across Damage and Economy
Before: all seeded items share powerScore 11.8 (entity-blind)
After: powerScore follows each item's baseDPS
Method: simulation - the walker impact needs e2e; M with walker risk
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/items.ts Economy produce: `const powerBreakdown = { dpsPower: 10.0, implicitAccuracyPower: 1.8, affixPower: 0 };`
// "base DPS 12.5 (avg dmg 10 x APS 1.25)" vs Damage dpsNote "15 x 0.8333"
instrument: coherence test: for every seeded item, economy.powerBreakdown.dpsPower == round(damage.baseDPS x 0.8) + walker run

title: Stop the Items tooltip calling every item a One-Handed Sword
body:
## Summary
The registered Tooltip still writes subHeaderLine "One-Handed Sword" and an iron-longsword description for every seeded item, armour and lightsabers included.

## Description
Since ca396b98 the tooltip's stat and implicit lines follow the Damage step, but subHeaderLine is still the literal "One-Handed Sword" (Tooltip produce in src/lib/catalog/pipelines/items.ts). The Base Type & Rarity produce in the same file derives subType, slot and equipType per entity (itemType, equipType). Fixed: build subHeaderLine from the Base Type step's subType + oneHanded/twoHanded, using the same hoisting pattern. Leave the description alone: it is template-held prose.

## Flow
- produce Tooltip for an armour seed
- subHeaderLine reads One-Handed Sword
- fix: derive it from the base type

## Expected impact
The tooltip header agrees with the Base Type step. Acceptance is unaffected (it reads only displayName, description and compareFields).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - tooltip header matches base type
Before: every seeded item: "One-Handed Sword"
After: per-item subtype
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/items.ts Tooltip produce `subHeaderLine: 'One-Handed Sword',`
Base Type produce `const itemType = effectiveValue<string>('itemType') ?? 'Sword';`
instrument: extend src/__tests__/catalog/items-tooltip-damage-coherence.test.ts with a subHeaderLine vs baseType.subType case

title: Draw the Material map tiles from REQUIRED_PBR_MAPS instead of a literal list
body:
## Summary
ItemMaterial's "Texture maps declared" panel iterates a literal ['Albedo','Normal','ORM','Height'], a third copy of the map set the checker and copy now share.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/ItemArt.tsx:148 hardcodes the four tiles. The checker requires REQUIRED_PBR_MAPS (itemsBespokeCheckers.ts:64), and since 86e2b616 the copy reads that constant too. A map added to the requirement would be graded but never get a tile. Fixed: tiles = [...REQUIRED_PBR_MAPS, ...optional extras], with the required ones marked.

## Flow
- add a required map to REQUIRED_PBR_MAPS
- the checker fails, and the panel shows no tile for the new map
- fix: derive the tiles

## Expected impact
The panel shows what the gate requires. Display only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one map-set authority
Before: 1 literal list in the view
After: 0
Method: simulation - a vi.mock test like itemCopyThresholds would gate it; budget went to higher-value items
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vi.mock REQUIRED_PBR_MAPS with an extra map, render ItemMaterial, expect its tile
